newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil eyes stake in Ukraine refineries.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil eyes stake in Ukraine refineries.

text.p: Russian oil company LUKoil is considering buying shares in three oil refineries in Ukraine, LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov said.

"At the moment we are looking at the possibility of taking a stake in the share capital of refineries in Drogobych, Kherson and Odessa," he told reporters on a flight from Chisinau to Moscow on Wednesday.
OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil already refines some of its oil at the Kremenchugsk plant in the Ukraine, Alekperov said.
He said LUKoil was not planning to take part in the privatisation of one of the largest Ukrainian refineries, Lisichansk (AO Lisichansknefteorgsintez).
The Ukrainian government plans to sell 45 percent of the refinery's shares to strategic investors on a competitive basis.
"We are not looking at Lisichansk, there are good Russian commercial structures in place there and they are able to realise their plans without our participation," Alekperov said.
There are six refineries in the Ukraine with annual capacity of around 60 million tonnes annually.
According to the Ukrainian Ministry of Statistics, Ukrainian plants refined 13.47 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996, down from 16.85 million in 1995.

In the first 10 months of last year the Kremenchugsk plant refined five million tonnes, Lisichansk 1.8 million tonnes, Khersonsk 1.1 million, Odessa 1.24 million, Drogobychsk 762,000 tonnes and Nadbornyansk 714,000, it said.
All Ukrainian refineries are at different stages of privatisation.
In December the Ukrainian cabinet decided to reform the oil and gas industry and create vertically integrated oil and gas companies.
On Tuesday Lukoil's Alekperov was in the Moldovan capital to open two Western-style gasoline stations.
He said the stations would be supplied by refineries in Russia, Belorussia and Ukraine.
